title: Token Reduction for Efficient Video Instance Segmentation with Transformers
abstract:
Video instance segmentation (VIS) provides detailed per-pixel scene understanding information across a temporal sequence. This temporally consistent segmentation is crucial for real-world applications such as robotic applications.
However, state-of-the-art approaches are computationally expensive and reducing this computational burden while maintaining high accuracy is critical for enabling their deployment on robots.
In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient token reduction approach for VIS which estimates the relevance of tokens in low-resolution feature layers and then maps this to higher level feature layers.
To be computationally efficient, we evaluate token uniqueness and assign scores at the lowest feature layer.
If a token is considered unique enough, we designate it as a \textit{reserved token} and then map it to the higher resolutions; this allows us to trade off reduced latency against performance. %in the attention process, with ranging impact on the average precision (AP) of the network.
We evaluate our approach on a complex real-world agricultural robotics dataset (BUP-ST20) as well as two common VIS datasets YouTube-VIS (YTVIS) 2019 and 2022.
On the BUP-ST20 with ResNet we are able to reduce inference time by 11\% and 20\% with an absolute degradation in performance of only 0.8 and 3.6 in AP for pruning ratios of 30% and 50%, respectively.  
On the most difficult YouTube-VIS dataset, YTVIS 2022, we show that for the ResNet model we are able to reduce inference time by 18% with an absolute degradation in performance of 4.1 AP. 
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to propose token reduction for video instance segmentation with transformer-based models.
